BERTScore wins. 5x sparser, 2.5x better shared token match, highest content focus. No gradient needed.

6-panel comparison (all methods professor requested)

Panels: A) IG+ABTT, B) BERTScore greedy, C) Optimal Transport, D) Attention cross-sim, E) DLA, F) Attention standalone. Top-5 cells highlighted.

LaBSE example. BERTScore (panel B) shows clean diagonal matches. DLA and Attention are denser/noisier.

Why not combine IG with the other methods?

Only Optimal Transport uses IG (as mass weights for how much importance each token carries). The other 4 non-IG methods are entirely gradient-free. This is intentional:

MethodUses IG?Importance signal
IG + ABTTYesIG is the method itself
BERTScoreNoCosine similarity + greedy matching
Optimal TransportYes|IG| as mass weights, cosine as transport cost
Attention cross-simNoSelf-attention diagonal
DLANoToken embedding norms
Attention standaloneNoAttention column-mean (received attention)

Why not add IG to the others?

  • BERTScore already wins without IG. It beats IG+ABTT on every metric (sparsity 0.08 vs 0.41, shared token 0.42 vs 0.17). Adding IG can only add noise.
  • IG highlights geometric properties, not semantic ones. IG attributes through the ABTT transform, so it highlights tokens that load onto removed principal components — a geometric artifact, not linguistic meaning. This is why the IG token matches often don’t make linguistic sense to human readers.
  • Being gradient-free is a feature. IG costs ~50 forward passes per example. BERTScore, DLA, and attention methods run in milliseconds on cached embeddings. For the webapp and live review, this matters.

Potential experiment: OT currently uses IG for mass weights. Testing OT with uniform or attention-based mass instead would show whether IG actually helps OT. The use_uniform=True flag already exists in the code but wasn’t evaluated.
